competencies.name: Consumer and user understanding
competencies.blurb: Who the user is, what they do, and why. Separates what you saw from what you assume.
competencies.demonstrate: Builds a defensible picture of a user from observation, and says what evidence is still missing.

competencies.name: Product discovery
competencies.blurb: Finding problems worth solving and testing the riskiest assumption cheaply.
competencies.demonstrate: Chooses the cheapest test for the riskiest assumption and acts on what it shows.

competencies.name: Product strategy
competencies.blurb: Choosing what to build, for whom, and what to leave out.
competencies.demonstrate: Defends a prioritisation and a trade-off to someone who disagrees.

competencies.name: Product design and UX
competencies.blurb: Whether a person can complete the task, understand the screen, and recover from errors.
competencies.demonstrate: Diagnoses a confusing flow and proposes a change tied to the user's task.

competencies.name: Product analytics
competencies.blurb: Metrics, funnels, cohorts and experiments, and what the numbers can and cannot say.
competencies.demonstrate: Diagnoses a metric move from evidence and separates correlation from cause.

competencies.name: Technical understanding
competencies.blurb: How the web, APIs, databases and services behave, and what that means for a product.
competencies.demonstrate: Explains a technical trade-off in plain language to a stakeholder and to an engineer.

competencies.name: System design
competencies.blurb: Requirements, scale, bottlenecks and failure, at the level a product manager needs.
competencies.demonstrate: Sketches a design from requirements and names where it breaks.

competencies.name: Product execution
competencies.blurb: Specs, roadmaps, estimates, launches and working with engineering.
competencies.demonstrate: Ships a scoped change with a clear spec, a plan and a way to know it worked.

competencies.name: Business and growth
competencies.blurb: Market size, pricing, unit economics and how products grow.
competencies.demonstrate: Builds a unit-economics argument and tests it against real constraints.

competencies.name: AI product management
competencies.blurb: What models can do, where they fail, what they cost, and how to evaluate them.
competencies.demonstrate: Decides whether an AI feature is worth building and how to measure it.

competencies.name: Product leadership
competencies.blurb: Influence without authority, stakeholder handling and decisions under disagreement.
competencies.demonstrate: Moves a group to a decision without relying on rank.

competencies.name: Communication and decision-making
competencies.blurb: Structured answers, clear writing, and showing your reasoning.
competencies.demonstrate: Explains a decision and its reasoning so others can challenge it.

levels.name: Understand
levels.line: Knows the definitions and can read a simple example.

levels.name: Apply
levels.line: Solves a guided exercise with a framework.

levels.name: Analyze
levels.line: Handles ambiguity, weighs trade-offs and diagnoses failures on their own.

levels.name: Demonstrate
levels.line: Solves an unfamiliar problem on their own, explains the reasoning and holds up to follow-up questions.
